messages:
Leah (PM): ok team — we need to lock the ordering for Optimize toolkit v1. Customers keep asking for quantization guidance, but infra wants batching + caching first. want to use RICE-ish tradeoff. quick take?
Ravi (Eng): +1 to having a principled RICE table. engineering effort for quantization recommendation engine looks medium, batching tuning is high (lots of infra work), caching MVP is low-medium depending on scope.
Elliot (ML): quant recommendations are high impact on cost for many customers (esp. 4-bit/8-bit flows). quality/regression risk though — need eval harness.
Maya (CS): customer asks: 3 enterprise customers want automated batching and cache hints to reduce bill variance. a few startups asked specifically for quant profiles to lower costs. both high signal.
Noah (SRE): caching has infra implications (cache invalidation, KV lifecycle). if we scope prototype as "prefix/KV cache suggestions" behind FF, infra lift is reasonable. full managed cache is much bigger.
Leah (PM): propose we do a 3-row RICE for the three knobs: quantization advisor, batching config autosuggest, prefix/KV cache prototype. Leah (PM): here's a quick RICE sketch — please react with adjustments: 
```
- Quantization advisor: Reach=medium, Impact=high, Confidence=0.6, Effort=3
- Batching autosuggest: Reach=high, Impact=medium, Confidence=0.7, Effort=5
- Cache prototype: Reach=medium, Impact=medium, Confidence=0.5, Effort=2
```
Ravi (Eng): numbers seem reasonable. Effort scale 1-5? if so caching is 2, quant advisor maybe 3-4 if we include eval infra.
Elliot (ML): Confidence on quant should be lower until we run more evals on common models/workloads — set conf=0.45 unless we commit to eval setup.
Maya (CS): from GTM POV, caching pilot is quickest to show cost wins to customers, especially those with high repeated prompts.
Noah (SRE): sequencing note: batching changes touch runtime scheduling and could affect latency SLOs. we should only roll batching after we have safe fallback and metrics.
Leah (PM): proposed sequencing based on RICE+risk: 1) Cache prototype behind FF (quick wins, low effort) 2) Quantization advisor v1 (recommendations + eval harness, medium effort) 3) Batching autosuggest + runtime safeguards (bigger infra).
Ravi (Eng): agree but suggest parallel tracks: infra starts safety/gating work for batching while ML/PD do quant evals and a small engineering team builds cache MVP. reduces end-to-end time.
Elliot (ML): we need launch criteria for quant advisor: a) show >=10% median token cost reduction on target workloads without >2% QA/quality regression, b) eval harness and canary on 5 customers.
Maya (CS): cache MVP launch criteria: measurable token savings for pilot customer (>=8%), clear TTL semantics, opt-in FF.
Noah (SRE): batching launch criteria: latency tail impact <5% and an automated fallback to single-request mode.
Leah (PM): good. next steps: Ravi to scope caching MVP (EOW), Elliot to propose eval plan (mid next week), Noah to draft batching safety checklist. I'll put this into a prioritization spreadsheet and run RICE numbers formally.
Ravi (Eng): noted. I'll flag any hidden infra blockers if estimate changes.
Elliot (ML): will pull example workloads from CS and surface failure modes.
Maya (CS): I'll line up pilot customers and draft messaging.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: optimize/pri/worksheet updated by Leah — 1813472100
Leah (PM): thanks — will sync in product stand. if anyone thinks order should be different, mention here. otherwise I'll publish to roadmap doc by EOD. :rocket:
